\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: verdana;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: verdana;\"\u003E1) Dialysis Disequilibrium syndrome? \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003EDialysis disequilibrium syndrome (DDS) refers to an array of neurological manifestations seen during or following dialysis, primarily after the new initiation of dialysis.However, it can also be seen in chronic dialysis patients who miss their regular dialysis treatments. This syndrome is thought to arise from fluid shifts during hemodialysis, causing cerebral edema and a wide variety of neurological symptoms. In continuous renal replacement therapies (CRRT), where fluid shift is limited, dialysis disequilibrium syndrome is rarely reported.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe common risk factors that predispose a patient to dialysis dysequilibrium syndrome are\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFirst hemodialysis treatment\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHigh blood urea nitrogen (BUN) (above 175 mg\/dL or 60 mmol\/L) before initiation of dialysis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EExtremes of age – children and elderly\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESudden change in dialysis regimen\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPre-existing neurological diseases such as stroke, malignant hypertension, head trauma, or seizure disorder\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPresence of other conditions causing cerebral edema (hyponatremia, hepatic encephalopathy)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EConditions causing increased permeability of the blood-brain barrier (sepsis, meningitis, encephalitis, hemolytic uremic syndrome, vasculitis) \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2) How spironolactone cause gynecomastea? \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; Spironolactone induces gynecomastia by decreasing testosterone production, increasing peripheral conversion of testosterone to estradiol, and displacing estradiol from sex hormone-binding globulin. \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; Learning points:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1) Learnt about indications and complications of Dialysis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2) Get know effects of long-term use of NSAIDS on kidney\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3)Learnt about Dialysis Disequilibrium syndrome \u0026nbsp;
